allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.9 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dark green leaves; yellow heads.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.note: The basal blade drawn as the stem's (spec rework E1), on a longer stalk, by eye from photographs.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.pattern.note: How PlantGen draws a divided leaf, a choice of the model's (spec rework P4): the leaf characters set a compound card's pattern, its leaflets or pinnae, the leaflets on each pinna, and whether its segments run together. A pinnate leaf's count says how it ends (odd-pinnate odd, even-pinnate even), so a flora's range is drawn as the nearest count of the right kind.

appearance.organs.flower.shape.disc.note: How PlantGen draws the daisy family's heads, a choice of the model's (spec rework P2): a head is laid out from its florets (`crate::capitula`), its phyllaries in rows round its foot, its receptacle domed as its shape says, its disc florets packed in a sunflower spiral and opening from the rim inward, rays round a radiate head, straps filling a ligulate one; an array of heads is a cluster of such heads (spec rework L1). Its size is its involucre's, as floras measure it, plus a ray on either side. The heights the shape words give the receptacle and the pappus lengths of crowns, scales and awns are the model's. A leaf's card is as wide, for its length, as the flora's blades; a head's size, and the share of its cluster it takes, follow from its involucre and rays.

appearance.organs.flower.shape.template.note: How PlantGen chooses an organ's card from the characters (species-spec pilot, 2026-10-14): only where no file at least as near chose one by hand.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.note: The blade drawn as a twice-divided leaf (spec rework E1), Abrams and Ferris's bipinnatifid blade of toothed, cut segments: about 5 pairs of primary segments, each cut into about 5 lobes, the end segment largest, by eye from photographs; its pattern from its characters by the rules at the flowering plants. Its segments run together along a winged rachis (confluent 0.6, by eye): the flora's blade is cut, not divided into leaflets, and the rule at the flowering plants that runs them together reads only a dissected one. Before, a five-lobed blade.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: an invasive, poisonous herb with ragged, deeply cut leaves and flat-topped clusters of yellow daisy heads. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.basal_length.note: How PlantGen's herb program sizes a herb's leaves from a flora's leaf lengths, a choice of the model's (spec rework E1 and E3): its longest stem and basal leaves as long as the longest leaf the flora gives, its lowest and topmost stem leaves shorter by the shortest's share of it, the card's petiole part of the length. Homed at the campanulids, where it holds for the daisy and carrot families and changes no other built-in species.

generator.params.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant bears both sexes, unless its taxa state it dioecious.

generator.params.leaves_per_node.note: What the words mean, as accounts of phyllotaxis such as Okabe and colleagues' use them: a spiral or two-ranked shoot bears one leaf at a node, a decussate one a pair and a whorled one three or more. A spiral turns about the golden angle (137.5 degrees) from node to node and two ranks half a turn; pairs and whorls alternate, each standing over the gaps of the one below, half the gap between its own leaves round (90 degrees for pairs). Three ranks turn a third of a turn, as their name says.

generator.params.sex.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant's sex is its own draw, dealt across a package's seeds so that both sexes grow; the typical plant (sex 0.5) is female, so it shows its fruit.

generator.params.stem_height.note: What the herb program's stem height means: each year's stems reach it at maturity, give or take height_spread, their flowers included, so a mature herb stands about as tall as a flora's usual height for the plant, read as the range's middle unless it names a typical height.

generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

generator.spreads.params.stem_height.note: What the herb program's stem height means: each year's stems reach it at maturity, give or take height_spread, their flowers included, so a mature herb stands about as tall as a flora's usual height for the plant, read as the range's middle unless it names a typical height.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
